name: Generic Object Playground
summary: See how one change flows through connected objects: Input A → Processor B (×2) → Display C.

simulation.title: Generic Object Playground
simulation.purpose: Show the basic concept: changing one object can change the output of connected objects.
simulation.agent_purpose: Predict and explain the consequences of changes before acting.
simulation.goal: Change Object A's value to 10 and show me what will happen.
simulation.benefit: The human can see the change propagate.
simulation.negative: Other objects using B's output may also change; if none are known, AFM says what it inspected rather than assume none exist.
simulation.unknown: Consumers of B's output outside this model are not known.
thinking: Task goal: “{goal}”. I capture the desired input, the desired output and observable success criteria. If the goal is broad I help define criteria, but I never present my proposals as human-approved.
I am AFM. My purpose is to predict and explain the consequences of changes before acting. I must be honest, report unknowns and ask for human approval before changing the playground.
I am in a simulated environment containing three connected objects.
The target is Object A. Nothing essential is missing: its new value is in the goal. If it were missing I would stop and ask.
I know Object A, Object B and Object C. A provides input to B; B provides output to C.
Object A holds a value, B processes it, and C displays the result. I may ask the LLM to explain these object types. The simulator reports A's value, B's rule (multiply by 2) and what C displays.
I can inspect the objects and simulate an update. A real change to the playground requires approval.
Simulate changing A, then predict B and C.
set_value on an input object is registered and allowed with approval; delete_object is prohibited, so any plan using it is rejected before prediction.
Predict A's new value, B's new output and what C will display.
Check that the simulated plan meets the goal and violates no configured rule. Execution requires approval.
Present the prediction: if I change A, what will B and C output? Ask: do you approve changing A in the simulated playground?
If approved and the playground has not changed, apply the reviewed action.
Inspect A, B and C and compare their observed values with the prediction.
Record whether A, B and C matched 10, 20 and 20; mismatches become lessons, not automatic retraining.
WIN only if my predictions matched (A=10, B=20, C=20), the agreed criterion (A holds 10) was observed, and every rule was respected.

demo_goals: Change Object A's value to 10 and show me what will happen.
definitions: Only Object A can be set directly. B's output and C's display are derived by configured behavior: B = A × 2, C shows B.
limitations: A three-object teaching model; every behavior is explicitly configured.
There are no unknown dependencies here on purpose, so it is the simplest example. Real environments are never this complete.

rules.text: Only the input object can be set directly; derived values (processor output, display) must not be edited.
rules.how: set_value accepts only an input object as target.

rules.text: Values must be whole numbers between -1000 and 1000.

rules.how: delete_object is prohibited and cannot be simulated or executed.

tools.name: set_value
tools.description: Set the value of an input object.
tools.reversible_note: The previous value can be set again.

tools.name: delete_object
tools.description: Delete an object. Prohibited by rule P3.

mock_llm_proposals.title: Delete Object B to simplify the chain

objects.name: Object A (Input)
objects.purpose: Holds a number that feeds the processor.
objects.behavior: Holds the value it is set to.

objects.name: Object B (Processor)
objects.purpose: Receives A's value and multiplies it by 2.
objects.behavior: output = input × factor, recomputed whenever its input changes (configured).

objects.name: Object C (Display)
objects.behavior: Shows the processor's output; refreshes immediately (configured).

relationships.description: B's output is what C displays.
